title: Tenant residency proofing templates for audit prep
content:
Purpose and scope

This working doc provides customer-facing templates + internal operator scripts for packaging auditable evidence that tenant data was processed and stored in the contracted region. It is intended for: onboarding engineers, engagement leads preparing customers for an audit, and SRE/ops staff gathering artifacts for compliance reviews.

Goals:
- Produce a minimal, repeatable evidence bundle that satisfies common enterprise audit asks (location logs, config snapshots, signed attestations).
- Reduce back-and-forth with legal by using standardized phrasing and checklist items.
- Provide operator scripts and step-by-step packaging instructions so evidence can be assembled reproducibly.

Important assumptions and constraints
- This doc focuses on region pinning/residency proof for Private/Dedicated deployments only (not Hosted multi-tenant audits).
- Evidence types vary by customer/regulator; consider this a baseline. Legal team may require additional fields (timestamps, signature format, KMS proofs).
- All artifacts should be redacted for PII where appropriate; see "Redaction guidance" section.

Contents overview (this doc)
1) Evidence bundle checklist (what to collect)
2) Standardized customer attestation template (language customers can sign)
3) Operator packaging script (bash + manifest format)
4) Sample telemetry queries 
5) Redaction + retention guidance
6) Escalation and review matrix

1) Evidence bundle checklist (baseline)
- Config snapshot: routing table / tenant pin settings / region tag values (export JSON/YAML).
- Deployment manifest: node region labels, availability zones, metadata showing model replicas pinned to region X.
- Access logs: gateway + control plane logs for time window requested (ISO8601 timestamps).
- Network egress summary: NAT gateway/egress IPs and flows limited to region endpoints.
- Storage proof: identifiers of storage buckets/volumes and their region metadata.
- Audit trace: operator actions (who changed pin, JIRA/PR link), and the associated console trace.
- Signed attestation: standard short-form statement from Redwood and from customer technical contact.
- Checksum manifest: sha256 sums for each artifact file.

Note: Each item should include: filename, creation timestamp, and a one-line description in the bundle manifest.

2) Customer attestation template (plain text)
[Customer letterhead optional]
Customer: <TENANT_NAME>
Customer contact: <NAME, EMAIL, PHONE>
Deployment ID / Tenant ID: <TENANT_ID>
Contracted residency region: <REGION_CODE / Cloud region>
Statement: \"As of <DATE>, <TENANT_NAME> confirms Redwood Inference was requested to pin all inference and storage resources for Tenant ID <TENANT_ID> to <REGION_CODE>, and that the tenant has been operating with those residency constraints. This attestation is provided to support audit activities and may be relied upon by Redwood and authorized auditors.\"
Signature: _______________________  Date: ____

Notes for legal: Attestation must be signed by authorized technical/business contact from the customer. Optionally notarized for higher assurance.

3) Operator packaging script (example, minimal)
# --- BEGIN Sample operator script ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
OUTDIR=\"residency-evidence-${TENANT_ID:-tenant123}-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)\"
mkdir -p \"$OUTDIR\"

# 1. export config snapshots
API_TOKEN=${API_TOKEN:-}
if [[ -z \"$API_TOKEN\" ]]; then echo \"ERROR: API_TOKEN required\"; exit 2; fi
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/tenants/${TENANT_ID}/pin-config\" > \"$OUTDIR/pin-config.json\"

# 2. collect node labels (kube or provisioner API)
kubectl get nodes -o json --selector=redwood-tenant=${TENANT_ID} > \"$OUTDIR/node-labels.json\" || true

# 3. fetch gateway logs for window
# accepts START/END as ISO timestamps
START=${START:-\"2024-09-01T00:00:00Z\"}
END=${END:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)}
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN\" \\
  \"https://logs.redwood.example/query?tenant=${TENANT_ID}&start=${START}&end=${END}\" > \"$OUTDIR/gateway-logs.json\"
# 4. collect storage metadata
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN\" \"https://storage.redwood.example/metadata?tenant=${TENANT_ID}\" > \"$OUTDIR/storage-metadata.json\"

# 5. create manifest and checksums
for f in \"$OUTDIR\"/*; do sha256sum \"$f\" >> \"$OUTDIR/checksums.txt\"; done
jq -n --arg tenant \"$TENANT_ID\" --arg date \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\" '{tenant:$tenant,generated:$date}' > \"$OUTDIR/manifest.json\"

tar -czf \"$OUTDIR.tar.gz\" -C \"$OUTDIR\" .
# --- END Sample operator script ---

Operator note: the script above is a minimal starting point. For high-assurance audits, capture raw syslogs, KMS entries (audit events only, not keys), and operator intervention records.

4) Sample telemetry queries (for SRE use)
- Count of requests routed outside contracted region in time window:
  SELECT count(*) FROM request_routes WHERE tenant_id = '<TENANT_ID>' AND routed_region != '<REGION_CODE>' AND ts BETWEEN '<START>' AND '<END>'
- Node allocation snapshot:
  SELECT node_id, region_label, pod_count FROM node_allocations WHERE tenant_id = '<TENANT_ID>'
- Storage bucket region lookup:
  SELECT bucket_id, region FROM storage_metadata WHERE tenant_id = '<TENANT_ID>'

5) Redaction guidance
- Never include raw user payloads. If logs contain user content, replace with token hashes (sha256) and provide a mapping only if legally required.
- PII fields: redact emails, phone numbers, national ids. Use consistent token like <REDACTED_EMAIL>.
- Crypto/keys: do not export private keys or raw HSM material. Include only KMS audit event ids and timestamps.

6) Retention and packaging policy for evidence bundles
- Default retention for evidence bundles: 90 days in the internal secure evidence vault, unless legal hold extends.
- For customer-requested exports, provide a time-limited signed URL (7 days) and require a receipt confirmation.
- Mark bundles with classification tag: SENSITIVE. Store in vault with access logging enabled.

7) Escalation and legal review matrix
- If any evidence shows a routing event outside contracted region: immediately notify Privacy & Legal, Eng PM for Private deployments, and customer technical contact.
- Severity levels:
  - Minor (single request out-of-region isolated to <1 hour): Ops review and corrective config rollback. Log and document in ticket.
  - Major (data persisted outside region or sustained routing >24h): Incident response, legal notification, customer outreach, and remediation plan.

8) Common customer questions (Q&A snippets for engagement leads)
Q: Will you include user content in the audit bundle?
A: No. We include metadata, routing logs (timestamps, request ids, region decisions), and storage identifiers. Raw user content is redacted by default; if customer requests otherwise we require explicit legal sign-off.

Q: How quickly can you produce these artifacts?
A: Minimal bundle: 1-2 business days. Expanded bundle (including raw syslogs and operator traces): 5-7 business days, depends on retention windows.

9) TODOs and open questions (for internal follow-up)
- [ ] Align manifest schema with Legal's evidence schema v1.3 (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Add KMS event sampling script that returns event ids and attestations without exposing key material.
- [ ] Template for notarized customer attestation.

Appendix: example bundle manifest (one-line per entry)
manifest_entries:
- pin-config.json | 2024-09-01T12:04:33Z | export of tenant pin config from control plane
- node-labels.json | 2024-09-01T12:05:10Z | kubernetes node region labels for tenant pods
- gateway-logs.json | 2024-09-01T12:00:00Z/2024-09-02T12:00:00Z | gateway routing decisions (ids only)
- storage-metadata.json | 2024-09-01T12:06:01Z | storage buckets with region tags
- customer-attestation.pdf | 2024-09-02T00:00:00Z | signed by customer technical authority
- checksums.txt | 2024-09-02T00:02:00Z | sha256 sums for file integrity

Contact and ownership

Escalation: eng-oncall -> privacy-legal -> product-lead (see linked_artifacts contact page)

End of doc.
